speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your acute diarrhea, how long have your symptoms been present, and have there been any episodes of blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI). The patient's recent treatment with levofloxacin and subsequent onset of watery diarrhea with cramping is highly suggestive of antibiotic-associated colitis. I will now confirm the duration of symptoms and rule out other causes before requesting specific stool testing. How many days have you been on the levofloxacin, and have you experienced fever or significant weight loss?
